subject: Post-call: model-fit & multilingual evals (EU + APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Müller <sofia.muller@globexretail.de>, Kenji Tanaka <kenji.tanaka@hikaru-retail.jp>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model-fit & multilingual evals (EU + APAC)

Hi Sofia / Kenji —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand the locales and quality priorities across your EU and APAC stores. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the evals running: 

What we heard
- Target languages: DE, FR, NL (priority EU); JA, KO, ZH (priority APAC).
- Primary use case: product QA + short-form customer responses (1-3 sentences typical).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 400ms for interactive flows; batch scoring allowed up to 2s.
- Volume: initial pilot ~500k tokens/week, expected growth to ~3-5M tokens/week.
- Data residency requirement: EU resident PII must remain in EU region for storage/processing.
- Key concerns: cross-locale quality regressions (esp. idiomatic JA/KO), hallucination tolerance for product facts, and tokenization edge cases for mixed-script inputs.

Recommended eval approach
1) Model candidates: RedBase-multilingual-7B-q4 (fast, good for short responses), Llama-2-13B-chat-q8 (higher quality for nuanced phrasing), and a larger candidate (Llama-2-70B-chat-8bit) for a head-to-head on worst-case QA items.
2) Prompt sets: attached is the initial prompt_set + target utterances (prompt_sets_globex_hikaru_v1.xlsx) covering the EU & APAC priority languages.
3) Benchmarks & rubric: I linked an internal benchmark folder with per-language baselines and the evaluation rubric (multilingual_eval_rubric_v1.pdf). Please review the rubric sections on hallucination tolerance and locale-specific fluency.
4) Quality/regression checks: we recommend running both automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE + a tailored factuality classifier) and a small human review panel (20-30 examples/lang) to flag idiomatic errors.

Next steps for us
- With your OK, we will: (a) spin up evaluation runs in EU and APAC regions using anonymized sample data, (b) produce a per-model per-language scorecard, and (c) highlight any regression vectors with suggested prompt/temperature mitigations.
- Can you confirm the prioritized languages and whether we can receive a 200-500 sample utterances per locale (anonymized) to seed the evals?
- Proposed follow-up: 30-minute tech deep dive next week to walk through the rubric and data handling. I’m available Tue/Wed 9-11am PT.

Attachments: prompt_sets_globex_hikaru_v1.xlsx, multilingual_eval_rubric_v1.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers:
- Confirmed languages: DE / FR are top priority, NL is lower priority for phase 1. For APAC, JA is top priority; KO/ZH we can include but may be phase 2.
- We can provide 300 anonymized sample utterances per priority locale (DE/FR/JA) by end of day Friday. They will be sanitized to remove PII.
- Data residency: we need processing and storage for EU samples to occur in an EU region. Will Redwood be able to run the eval stack inside an EU-only environment?

Question: can you share a rough timeline for the evaluation runs (how long to get back a scorecard)? Also, what controls will you put in place for the sample data (retention, deletion)?

Sofia

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model-fit & multilingual evals (EU + APAC)

Hi Sofia — thanks, that plan works. Quick answers and a proposed timeline: 

EU-only processing
- Yes — we can run the evaluation pipeline inside an EU-hosted cluster (we'll provision in eu-west1). For this pilot we will not persist raw samples outside the EU region. Results scorecards (aggregates and per-example ids) can be delivered to a shared folder you control.
- Retention: we propose a 30-day retention for intermediate artifacts, after which raw sample artifacts will be purged unless you request archiving. We will include deletion confirmations in the delivery notes.

Timeline
- Day 0-2: ingest sample bundle and sanity-check (tokenization, script detection).
- Day 3-4: automated runs (per-model per-language) + initial metric report.
- Day 5-7: human review on flagged items + final scorecard and playbook with recommended prompt mitigations and quantization profiles.

Quality/regression guardrails
- We'll run a focused factuality classifier on product-name / SKU responses and surface any hallucination clusters. For idiomatic errors in JA/KO we'll surface common failure modes and propose prompt tuning plus a small in-context example bank.

Attachments (re-attached): prompt_sets_globex_hikaru_v1.xlsx, multilingual_eval_rubric_v1.pdf
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Model-Benchmarks

Next steps
1) Sofia: confirm EU-only processing and confirm sample delivery timeline (you mentioned Fri).
2) Kenji: if Hikaru is participating for JA, can we get 200 sample JA utterances?
3) I’ll schedule the tech deep dive for Tue 9am PT unless you prefer another time.
